rationale:
Issue #69 reports that randomSample traps when Double.random(in: 0..<1) yields 0, because Double.log(0.0) is -inf and Int(-inf) is not representable. The minimized production patch is a single 2-line hunk in Sources/Algorithms/RandomSample.swift that shifts the sampled value from [0,1) to (0,1] via `1 - .random(in: 0..<1)` in nextOffset (removing the log(0) case) and in nextW (keeping w != 0 so the divisor .log(1 - w) is nonzero), which is exactly the defect and mechanism described in the issue and PR #70 body. Both changed lines address the same zero-sample root cause; there is no refactor, formatting, feature extension, documentation, or configuration content, and the production and test changes are separated (production_fix.patch vs trigger-tests.patch). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test testRandomSampleZeroRandom from the same fixing commit, using the exact SplitMix64 seed 0x61c8864680b583eb named in the issue reproducer together with the pre-existing randomSample(count:using:) API and pre-existing test fixtures, so it does not depend on any API introduced by the fix. Traceability is fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue with verified_fix_issue_numbers=[69], matching allowed_root_cause_ids, and active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this is not a duplicate. Machine-generated strict evidence passes all gates both originally and post-minimization: build on both revisions, unique selector, buggy differential failure on the declared selector, deterministic fingerprints over 3 repetitions, fixed-revision isolated/suite/reversed runs clean, and buggy full-suite failures limited to the reproduced trigger.

Issue #69 reports that randomSample traps when Double.random(in: 0..<1) yields 0, because Double.log(0.0) is -inf and Int(-inf) is not representable. The minimized production patch is exactly that defect's fix: two lines in Sources/Algorithms/RandomSample.swift shifting the sampled value from [0,1) to (0,1] via `1 - .random(in: 0..<1, using: &rng)` in nextW and nextOffset, addressing both log(0) = -inf and the w == 0 case that makes log(1 - w) zero (division by zero), as described in PR #70's body. Traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR #70 -> issue #69. The patch is a single hunk, production-only, 2 additions/2 deletions, with no refactor, formatting, feature, documentation, or configuration change (original_hunk_count=1, retained=1, removed=0; post_minimization_validation PASS). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit: testRandomSampleZeroRandom uses the pre-existing SplitMix64 helper and pre-existing fixtures c and k, calls the pre-existing randomSample(count:using:) API, and reproduces the issue reporter's own seed 0x61c8864680b583eb; it introduces no API created by the fix. Machine-generated strict evidence passes all gates on both the original and post-minimization configurations: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (1 declared, 1 valid, 1 unique), trigger.buggy_differential reproducing Tests/SwiftAlgorithmsTests/RandomSampleTests.swift::testRandomSampleZeroRandom, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions), matrix.complete (32 runs), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so apple/swift-algorithms#69 is not a duplicate of any active registry entry, and it is the sole allowed_root_cause_ids value.

The trigger contains no assertion and relies on abnormal process termination on the buggy revision; its failing signal depends on the harness treating the trap as a failure, and strict evidence reports this as satisfied without exposing the failure fingerprint itself.
The trigger's reproduction depends on SplitMix64 emitting 0 first for the hardcoded seed, so it is sensitive to any future change in that test-only generator helper.
The nextW change alters generated sampling sequences for seeded runs; the full suite is green on the fixed revision, but downstream tests comparing exact sampled output would be seed-sensitive.
The fix commit is one of four commits in PR #70 (later commits switch to log(onePlus:) and add clamping), so the accepted revision pair predates the final upstream form of this code.
